Definition: diminutive of G5557; a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin:--gold.
BiblicalUsage: Gold in the New Testament is what people reach for first and what God tests most: Peter has no silver or gold to give the lame man, but he gives him Jesus. Paul tells women not to dress in gold, and Hebrews lists the golden censer and the ark overlaid with gold. Peter says faith is more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tried with fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gold is the Bible's test of what we value, because it shines and it lasts and it still cannot save. The lame man got something better than gold, and so does every believer. I hold that faith tried by fire is the only gold that survives the testing.
